svg.title: Natural gradient
svg.desc: Contours of the average negative log-likelihood of a normal model for 200 points with mean about 2 and standard deviation about 0.44, in the (μ, σ) plane. From the start (−1, 3), plain gradient descent in (μ, σ) (solid orange) and in (μ, log σ) (dashed orange) take visibly different paths to the same answer. Natural gradient descent (blue), which rescales the gradient by the inverse Fisher matrix, takes the same path in both coordinate systems: it keeps the Gaussian wide while it moves the mean, and narrows it at the end.
svg.text: Fitting a Gaussian: plain gradient against natural gradient
